arxiv-2108-06495.title: On Column Competent Matrices and Linear Complementarity Problem
arxiv-2108-06495.creator: A. Dutta, R. Jana, A. K. Das
arxiv-2108-06495.description: Abstract We revisit the class of column competent matrices and study some matrix theoretic properties of this class. The local w w -uniqueness of the solutions to the linear complementarity problem can be identified by the column competent matrices. We establish some new results on w w -uniqueness properties in connection with column competent matrices.

arxiv-2307-05143.title: Process-Algebraic Models of Multi-Writer Multi-Reader Non-Atomic Registers
arxiv-2307-05143.creator: Myrthe Spronck, Bas Luttik
arxiv-2307-05143.description: Abstract We present process-algebraic models of multi-writer multi-reader safe, regular and atomic registers. We establish the relationship between our models and alternative versions presented in the literature. We use our models to formally analyse by model checking to what extent several well-known mutual exclusion algorithms are robust for relaxed atomicity requirements.

arxiv-2307-15803.title: Coordination Sequences of Periodic Structures are Rational via Automata Theory
arxiv-2307-15803.creator: Eryk Kopczyński
arxiv-2307-15803.description: Abstract We prove the conjecture of Grosse-Kunstleve et al. that coordination sequences of periodic structures in n n -dimensional Euclidean space are rational. This has been recently proven by Nakamura et al.; however, our proof is a straightforward application of classic techniques from automata theory.

arxiv-2309-00043.title: New families of scale separated vacua
arxiv-2309-00043.creator: Rafael Carrasco,
arxiv-2309-00043.description: Abstract IFT-UAM/CSIC-23-101 Massive type IIA flux compactifications of the form AdS {}_{4}\times X_{6} , where X_{6} admits a Calabi–Yau metric and O6-planes wrapping three-cycles, display families of vacua with parametric scale separation between the compactification scale and the AdS 4 radius, generated by an overall rescaling of internal four-form fluxes.

arxiv-2311-00130.title: Search for an exotic decay of the Higgs boson into a \PZ \PZ boson and a pseudoscalar particle in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2311-00130.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . A search for an exotic decay of the Higgs boson to a \PZ boson and a light pseudoscalar particle ( \Pa \Pa ), decaying to a pair of leptons and a pair of photons, respectively, is presented. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV , collected with the CMS detector at the LHC and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv .

arxiv-2510-13780.title: Macro-Level Correlational Analysis of Mental Disorders: Economy, Education, Society, and Technology Development
arxiv-2510-13780.creator: Yingzhi Tao 1, Chang Yang
arxiv-2510-13780.description: Abstract This paper quantifies the age-stratified global burden of four mental disorders in 27 regions from 1990 to 2021 using GBD 2021. To put it in detail, it links the age-standardized years of disability adjustment with 18 world development indicators across economic, educational, social and information technology sectors.

arxiv-2510-20108.title: Why Prototypes Collapse: Diagnosing and Preventing Partial Collapse in Prototypical Self-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2510-20108.creator: Gabriel Y. Arteaga 1 and Marius Aasan 1 and Rwiddhi Chakraborty 2 and Martine Hjelkrem-Tan 1 and Thalles Silva 3 and Michael Kampffmeyer 2 and Adín Ramírez Rivera 1 gabrieya@uio.no mariuaas@uio.no rwiddhi.chakraborty@uit.no matan@uio.no thalles.silva@students.ic.unicamp.br michael.c.kampffmeyer@uit.
arxiv-2510-20108.description: Abstract Prototypical self-supervised learning methods consistently suffer from partial prototype collapse, where multiple prototypes converge to nearly identical representations. This undermines their central purpose—providing diverse and informative targets to guide encoders toward rich representations—and has led practitioners to over-parameterize prototype sets or add ad-hoc regularizers, which mitigate symptoms rather than address the root cause.

pmc-13536071.title: Adapting multicomponent tobacco use treatment strategies for implementation in the Lebanese primary healthcare system: a mixed-methods study
pmc-13536071.creator: Dima S Bteddini, Catherine El Ashkar, Ruba Abla, Magda Montague, Lama El Kadi, Tamar Kabakian-Khasholian, Ji-Hyun Lee, Ryan Theis, Jihan Khaywa, Derek Li, Randa S Hamadeh, Kenneth Ward, Mona H Osman, Donna R Shelley, Maya Romani, Rima Nakkash, Ramzi G Salloum, Jennifer H LeLaurin
pmc-13536071.description: AbstractIntroductionTobacco use treatment (TUT) remains largely absent from Lebanon’s primary healthcare system, even though smoking prevalence ranks among the highest in the region. Although Lebanon has ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, TUT has not been integrated into routine care. This study describes the adaptation of evidence-based, phone-delivered TUT strategies for integration within Lebanon’s primary healthcare network.

pmc-13595797.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPerioperative bleeding is a common surgical complication and a frequently used outcome in randomized trials; however, its definition and analysis are not straightforward and have important implications for trial design, statistical power and interpretation of treatment effect.

pmc-13680053.title: A novel strategy for reconstruction of AORI type III proximal tibial defects
pmc-13680053.creator: Xingzhen Li, Qing Han, Xue Zhao, Jinbo Zhang, Qian Wan, Zhennan Gan, Xiaonan Wang, Xin Zhao, Hao Chen, Aobo Zhang, Jincheng Wang
pmc-13680053.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsFor cases of Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) type III proximal tibial defects with intact medial collateral ligaments (MCLs), knee reconstruction is conventionally performed using semi-constrained prostheses with stemmed tibial components in conjunction with cones or sleeves. This study aimed to reconstruct AORI type III tibial defects using a 3D-printed extension-stem augment, followed by surface-type knee reconstruction to achieve long-term stability and promising clinical outcomes.MethodsA patient-specific porous extension-stem augment was designed based on the defect morphology.
